title: Operator live-trace collection and rollback playbook
author: Lena Ortiz
content:
Summary

This runbook describes the on-call operator workflow for collecting live inferences traces (live-traces), extracting high-fidelity kernel/dispatch telemetry, performing a safe canary or full rollback of runtime/kernel changes, and verifying SLA preservation. It is intended for SREs and runtime engineers running live incidents where a kernel, scheduler, or runtime rollout is suspected of degrading latency, throughput, or correctness.

Scope

- Applies to the production inference runtime (service: inference-runtime-v2) across Hosted and Dedicated clusters.
- Covers: live-trace capture, short-term retention, signal triage, automated rollback criteria, manual rollback steps, verification, and post-incident actions.
- Does NOT cover model artifact rollbacks or customer data access procedures. See the release gating doc for those flows.

Ownership and escalation

- Primary owner: eng-serving-runtime oncall (team roster: runtime-sre@redwood.com).
- Fallback: runtime-core engineers (runtime-core@redwood.com).
- Pager escalation: follow the oncall rotation. If SLA impact > 5% error budget within 30m, notify on-call manager and SRE lead.

Signals / When to run this playbook

Run this playbook when one or more of the following are observed:

- Tail P99 latency for text.generate or chat.stream exceeds baseline by > 40% for 10+ minutes.
- Error rate (5xx or RPC timeouts) increases above 0.5% absolute and persists 5+ minutes.
- Sudden spike in kernel-level timeouts or NVLink retransmits reported by kernel telemetry.
- Canary or experimental rollout shows divergent latency/cost compared to control group.

Prerequisites and quick checks

- Ensure you have kube and opscli access: kube-context with cluster-admin and opscli >= v1.12.
- Confirm active trace retention window: default retention for live-traces is 2 hours. If the incident is older, check archived trace store (s3://redwood-runtime-traces/archived).
- Check current rollout state: opscli rollout status inference-runtime-v2 --environment=prod
- Confirm SLOs: generation P95 < 200ms, P99 < 850ms, error rate < 0.5%.

Step A — Rapid triage: collect lightweight indicators (0–5 minutes)

1) Pull high-level SLO metrics and recent deployment metadata:

- Grafana panels: inference/slo-overview-prod, kernel/dispatch-health, scheduler/admission-rate.
- CLI queries (examples):
  - opscli metrics query "sum(rate(inference_generation_latency_ms_p99[5m]))" --env=prod
  - kubectl -n runtime get pods -l app=inference-runtime-v2 -o wide

2) Identify suspect deployment(s) and kernel artifact versions:

- opscli rollout list --service=inference-runtime-v2 --env=prod
- If a kernel or runtime image was deployed in the last 30–120 minutes, note the image tag and rollout id.

3) Open a live incident channel and annotate: #inc-runtime-prod and add the rollout id, observed metric deltas, and time window.

Step B — Live-trace capture (5–30 minutes)

Goal: capture a set of 200–500 representative trace samples covering slow tails and error cases. Keep captures focused to reduce overhead.

1) Select 2–3 representative frontends or routes (e.g., /v1/generate, /v1/chat/stream).
2) Use the trace capture command to start an on-host sampler:

- opscli trace start --service inference-runtime-v2 --routes "/v1/generate,/v1/chat/stream" --duration 30m --sampler=error-first --max-samples 500 --label incident=<INCIDENT_ID>

3) For immediate collection (when rollout is live), prefer error-first sampling to ensure tokenization/kernel failures are captured. For tail-latency troubleshooting, use tail-latency sampler: --sampler=latency-tail --threshold-ms=500.

4) Monitor capture progress and backpressure:

- opscli trace status <trace-id>
- If capture fails due to agent overload, reduce duration to 10m and retry.

5) After capture completes, snapshot raw trace bundle to archive for triage:

- opscli trace export <trace-id> --dest s3://redwood-runtime-traces/incidents/<INCIDENT_ID>/raw.zip

Step C — Signal enrichment and quick attribution (30–90 minutes)

1) Enrich traces with kernel and scheduler telemetry (automatic for live-traces). Use the trace viewer filters:

- Kernel step durations: kernel.exec_ms, kernel.kv_lookup_ms, kernel.copy_ms
- Scheduling signals: scheduler.queue_ms, admission.rejected_count, preempt.count

2) Run the quick attribution queries (examples):

- opscli trace query --trace-id <trace-id> --filter "kernel.exec_ms > 200" --aggregate "count(),p99(kernel.exec_ms)"
- jq filter for trace bundle: jq '.spans[] | select(.tags.kernel_exec_ms>200) | {pod:.host, span:.name, t:.duration_ms}' traces.json

3) Look for these common failure modes:

- Kernel regression: p99 kernel.exec_ms increased while scheduling queue_ms stays stable.
- Admission/backpressure: admission.rejected_count spike, long scheduler.queue_ms leading to timeout.
- KV-cache hot miss storm: many large kv_lookup_ms peaks correlated with model switching.

Decision point: do we rollback?

Rollback is recommended when:

- A deterministic regression is attributed to a specific kernel or runtime image AND
- The regression meets business impact thresholds (P99 > 40% above baseline or error delta > 0.3% absolute for 15+ minutes) OR
- Canary group divergence > 25% on cost/latency and automated rollback policy (canary-fidelity-policy) tripped.

Step D — Automated canary rollback (safe, fast)

If the rollout was governed by opscli and automatic canary policies are enabled, trigger the automated rollback first so the system can restore traffic gradually:

- opscli rollout abort --rollout-id <id> --reason "auto-rollback: runtime P99 regression"

Verify progress: opscli rollout status <id> should show traffic shifting back to previous replica set. Monitor SLOs for 5–20 minutes after rollback completion.

Step E — Manual rollback (when automated path is not available or failed)

1) Pre-rollback checks:

- Ensure the prior image is available in registry: docker pull registry.redwood.com/runtime:<previous-tag>
- Confirm db/config compatibility for hot rollback (consult runtime-hot-compat-list).

2) Manual rollback via opscli (preferred):

- opscli rollout promote --service inference-runtime-v2 --image registry.redwood.com/runtime:<previous-tag> --env prod --strategy=rolling --max-unavailable=1 --max-surge=1 --annotate "rollback:incident=<INCIDENT_ID>"

3) K8s direct rollback (only if opscli path unavailable):

- kubectl -n runtime set image deploy/inference-runtime-v2 inference-runtime=registry.redwood.com/runtime:<previous-tag>
- kubectl -n runtime rollout status deploy/inference-runtime-v2 --timeout=10m

4) If the rollback cannot complete due to image pull or resource constraints, follow the escalation steps:
  - Open a high-priority ticket to infra-ops and ping #infra-urgent. Include deployment error logs and node pressure reports.

Step F — Verification and validation (5–30 minutes)

1) Immediate checks (0–5 minutes after new pods become Ready):

- smoke: run integration smoke suite against canary endpoints (smoke-cli run runtime/basic-smoke --env=prod --sample=20)
- sanity logs: kubectl -n runtime logs -l app=inference-runtime-v2 --tail=200 | grep -i error | head -n 50

2) SLO and telemetry validation (5–30 minutes):

- Confirm P95/P99 and error rate trending back to baseline via Grafana.
- Verify kernel metrics: kernel.exec_ms p99 reduced to baseline.
- Validate admission queue and preemption counters normalized.

3) If metrics do not stabilize after rollback, revert the rollback and trigger deep investigation with runtime-core (see Post-incident actions).

Step G — Post-incident actions

1) Record incident timeline and actions in the incident tracker; attach trace bundle and opscli logs.
2) Create an action item to run replay experiments against the archived trace set in the lab environment (lab replay tag: incident-<INCIDENT_ID>-replay).
3) If rollback was caused by a kernel change, schedule a kernel-stage regression hunt: owner runtime-kernel-team, priority P1, due within 3 business days.

Configuration reference (threshold table)

- Metric | Alert threshold | Operator action
- P99 latency (generation) | > 40% baseline for 10m | Run this playbook, collect traces, consider rollback
- Error rate (5xx) | > 0.5% absolute for 5m | Collect traces, check canary, consider rollback
- Admission rejects | > 1000/min | Inspect scheduler, consider capacity adjustments
- Kernel exec p99 | > 200 ms 

Quick commands and parsable examples

- List recent rollouts:
  - opscli rollout list --service inference-runtime-v2 --limit 10 --env=prod
- Start trace capture (JSON example):
  - opscli trace start --json '{"service":"inference-runtime-v2","routes":["/v1/generate"],"duration_mins":20,"sampler":"latency-tail","max_samples":300,"label":"incident-1234"}'
- Export and unzip traces locally:
  - aws s3 cp s3://redwood-runtime-traces/incidents/incident-1234/raw.zip ./ && unzip raw.zip

Known limitations and safety notes

- Live trace captures produce additional overhead on runtime pods; prefer short captures and avoid simultaneous capture on all nodes.
- Rollback does not revert model artifacts; ensure model compatibility with previous runtime.
- For multi-region incidents, rollback by region to limit blast radius.

Verification checklist to close the incident (all items required)

- [ ] Trace bundle captured and archived (s3 path noted)
- [ ] Rollback (automated or manual) executed if criteria met
- [ ] SLO metrics returned to baseline for 30 minutes or incident escalated
- [ ] Incident channel annotated with rollout id and action history
- [ ] Post-incident replay scheduled and owner assigned

Appendix: helpful queries and field definitions

- kernel.exec_ms: time spent executing kernel compute (ms)
- kernel.kv_lookup_ms: average per-request KV cache lookup time (ms)
- scheduler.queue_ms: time spent waiting for slot assignment (ms)
- admission.rejected_count: count of requests rejected by admission controller

- Example Kibana/Kusto query for tail traces:
  - "service:inference-runtime-v2 AND span.duration_ms:>400" | sort by @timestamp desc | limit 500

- Artifact registry locations: registry.redwood.com/runtime:<tag> and registry.redwood.com/kernel:<tag>
